tasks.notes: plan-defect: leg (a) contradicts its own Machine clause on the entry count. The leg's fixture is run:open, a red driver:exam-run for task 1 naming THING, then a same-kind same-cmd event with exit 1 — that is TWO reds, and M1 says derive_catches 'judges every red driver run that names a test path'. So the row carries two entries: ['stayed-red', 'no-green'] (the trailing red has no later same-run event). The leg's 'yields exactly one reds entry ... outcome stayed-red' can only hold if a trailing red is left unjudged, which would contradict M1 and the Claim's headline ('every red is judged') and would also silently change record-ful runs — the identical BASE shape in the existing test_g_next_same_run_still_red_is_stayed_red yields two entries at BASE and still does. I implemented M1/the Claim as written: reds[0] is task 1 / path THING / outcome stayed-red with catches == {}, and reds[1] is the trailing red's no-green. If the peer's exam asserts the count with _only(row['reds']) for leg (a) it will fail on the second entry; the fix is in the leg text, not in the implementation.
